prompt: According to frontier orbital theory, what determines whether an electrocyclic reaction is conrotatory or disrotatory?

choices.text: The symmetry of the polyene HOMO
The symmetry of the polyene LUMO
choices.why: The HOMO holds the highest-energy, most loosely held electrons, which are most easily moved during reaction; its symmetry decides.

choices.text: The number of methyl groups on the terminal carbons
choices.why: Substituents show which way the orbitals rotated, but the rotation itself is set by the HOMO's symmetry.

choices.text: Which product is more stable
choices.why: Stability can decide between two allowed products (Exercise 30.3.2), but the HOMO's symmetry decides the rotation.

explanation: The stereochemistry of an electrocyclic reaction is determined by the symmetry of the polyene HOMO. Its electrons are the highest-energy, most loosely held electrons, and so are most easily moved during reaction.

prompt: Which electron configuration is used to find the HOMO for a thermal electrocyclic reaction?

choices.text: The ground-state configuration
The excited-state configuration
choices.why: The excited-state configuration is used for photochemical reactions.

choices.text: Either one; both give the same HOMO
choices.why: Excitation moves an electron into a new orbital, so the ground-state and excited-state HOMOs differ.

choices.text: The configuration of the cyclic product
choices.why: The HOMO of the polyene reactant is what matters.

explanation: For thermal reactions, the ground-state electron configuration is used to identify the HOMO; for photochemical reactions, the excited-state configuration is used.

prompt: The ground-state HOMO of a conjugated triene has lobes of like sign on the same side of the molecule at its two ends. What kind of thermal ring-closure does this predict?

choices.text: Disrotatory
Conrotatory
choices.why: Conrotatory motion is needed when like-sign lobes are on opposite sides, as in a conjugated diene's ground-state HOMO.

choices.text: Suprafacial
choices.why: Suprafacial and antarafacial describe cycloadditions and sigmatropic rearrangements, not electrocyclic rotation.

choices.text: No ring-closure; it is symmetry-disallowed
choices.why: Thermal cyclization of 2,4,6-octatriene is observed, and it is disrotatory.

explanation: Like-sign lobes on the same side require the two ends to rotate in opposite directions. This disrotatory ring-closure is exactly what is seen when 2,4,6-octatriene is heated (Figure 30.3.1).

choices.text: In a conrotatory fashion
In a disrotatory fashion
choices.why: Disrotatory is the thermal mode for trienes. The ground-state HOMO of a conjugated diene predicts conrotatory motion.

choices.text: It doesn't open; heating closes 2,4-hexadiene to the cyclobutene instead
choices.why: Because of the position of the equilibrium, the diene reaction is seen only in the cyclobutene → diene direction.

choices.text: Suprafacially
choices.why: Electrocyclic reactions are described as conrotatory or disrotatory; suprafacial is a cycloaddition term.

explanation: The ground-state HOMO of a conjugated diene predicts conrotatory motion. Because the equilibrium favors the open-chain diene, the reaction is observed as ring-opening: 3,4-dimethylcyclobutene opens in a conrotatory fashion (Figure 30.3.2).

prompt: How many electron pairs (double bonds) undergo bond reorganization in the electrocyclic ring-closure of 2,4,6-octatriene?
explanation: 2,4,6-Octatriene has three double bonds, so three electron pairs reorganize. An odd number of pairs means a disrotatory thermal reaction.

prompt: How many electron pairs (double bonds) undergo bond reorganization in the 3,4-dimethylcyclobutene ⇄ 2,4-hexadiene electrocyclic reaction?
explanation: The diene side has two double bonds, so two electron pairs reorganize. An even number of pairs means a conrotatory thermal reaction.

prompt: Which statement gives the section's rule for thermal electrocyclic reactions?

choices.text: An even number of electron pairs reacts conrotatory; an odd number reacts disrotatory
An even number of electron pairs reacts disrotatory; an odd number reacts conrotatory
choices.why: This is reversed. The diene (two pairs) is conrotatory and the triene (three pairs) is disrotatory.

choices.text: All thermal electrocyclic reactions are disrotatory
choices.why: Dienes open and close by a conrotatory path; only trienes are disrotatory.

choices.text: Ring-closures are disrotatory and ring-openings are conrotatory
choices.why: The mode depends on the number of electron pairs, not on direction: a reaction and its reverse follow the same path.

explanation: There is an alternating relationship: polyenes with an even number of electron pairs undergo thermal electrocyclic reactions in a conrotatory sense, and those with an odd number in a disrotatory sense.

prompt: What product forms when (2Z,4Z,6Z)-2,4,6-octatriene is heated, and by which path?

choices.text: cis-5,6-Dimethyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene, by disrotatory closure
trans-5,6-Dimethyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene, by conrotatory closure
choices.why: Conrotatory closure would give the trans product, but a triene (three electron pairs) reacts thermally by a disrotatory path.

choices.text: trans-5,6-Dimethyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene, by disrotatory closure
choices.why: Disrotatory closure of the 2Z,4Z,6Z isomer puts the methyl groups cis, as in Exercise 30.3.1.

choices.text: cis-5,6-Dimethyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene, by conrotatory closure
choices.why: Thermal triene closures are disrotatory, and conrotatory closure of this isomer would give the trans product.

explanation: Exercise 30.3.1: disrotatory closure of (2Z,4Z,6Z)-2,4,6-octatriene gives cis-5,6-dimethyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene; conrotatory closure would give the trans isomer. A thermal triene reaction is disrotatory, so the cis product forms.

prompt: Conrotatory opening of trans-3,4-dimethylcyclobutene could give either (2E,4E)- or (2Z,4Z)-2,4-hexadiene. Why is only the 2E,4E isomer obtained?

choices.text: Both paths are symmetry-allowed, and the more stable of the two allowed products forms
The path to the 2Z,4Z isomer is symmetry-disallowed
choices.why: Both conrotatory paths have the correct symmetry, so both are allowed.

choices.text: The 2Z,4Z isomer would need disrotatory motion
choices.why: Both products arise from conrotatory openings, rotating in one direction or the other.

choices.text: Heat favors the less stable of the two allowed products
choices.why: It is the reverse: the more stable allowed product, (2E,4E)-2,4-hexadiene, is the one formed.

explanation: Exercise 30.3.2: both conrotatory openings of trans-3,4-dimethylcyclobutene are symmetry-allowed. In practice the more stable of the two allowed products, (2E,4E)-2,4-hexadiene, is formed.

prompt: Why do a conjugated diene and a conjugated triene react with opposite stereochemistry in thermal electrocyclic reactions?

choices.text: Their HOMOs have different symmetries: the diene HOMO's terminal lobes of like sign are on opposite sides, the triene HOMO's on the same side
The diene reacts through its LUMO and the triene through its HOMO
choices.why: In both cases the thermal reaction is governed by the ground-state HOMO.

choices.text: The diene ring is strained and the triene ring is not
choices.why: Strain affects where the equilibrium lies, not whether the motion is conrotatory or disrotatory.

choices.text: The diene reaction is photochemical and the triene reaction is thermal
choices.why: Both are being compared under thermal conditions; the difference comes from HOMO symmetry.

explanation: The diene opens and closes by a conrotatory path, whereas the triene opens and closes by a disrotatory path. This is due to the different symmetries of the diene and triene HOMOs.
